files.label: Your own sites
files.description: One row per site: name, kind (supplier, port, warehouse, store, dark store or customer area), latitude, longitude, and optionally teuPerDay, floorArea, population and from (the sites it is supplied from, separated by |).

files.label: Your travel times
files.description: One row per link: from and to (site names), time door to door (1:25, 85 min or 1 h 25 min), and optionally kilometres, when (any, peak, midday or night) and a note.

files.label: Your fleet operator
files.description: A haulier's trucks: one or two truck sizes with their costs, depots with their trucks, and the lanes it carries by origin and destination.

scenarios.name: Chokepoint disruption
scenarios.description: Fewer ships come through a strait or canal for a while, and the ports that depend on it receive less. Watch warehouse stock fall and customers' orders wait, then recover.
effects: Each port's arrivals fall by its share of ships through the chokepoint times the cut, for the chosen days.
Its warehouses stop ordering the cargo that will not come while the cut lasts.
Demand everywhere changes by the share given while the cut lasts (none by default).

scenarios.name: Chokepoint disruption, cargo diverted
scenarios.description: Fewer ships come through a strait or canal for a while, and part of the cargo kept out lands at one or two ports outside it instead and is carried inland by road from there. Watch that port's anchorage and yard, and the vehicles on its lanes.
effects: Each port's arrivals fall by its share of ships through the chokepoint times the cut.
The diverted cargo arrives at the chosen port; its warehouses order it from there, and those lanes hire vehicles for it.
The chosen port's berths keep their capacity, or take the capacity given from the disruption's first day to the end of the run.
Demand everywhere changes by the share given while the cut lasts (none by default).

scenarios.name: Road closure
scenarios.description: A road is closed, or restricted, for a while. Its vehicles wait for it to reopen, take a detour, or the site it leads to orders from its other sources. Watch that site's stock fall, the lane's vehicles get busy and the goods wait where they are.
effects: Closed, the lane loads only its open share; vehicles already on the road finish their trips.
On a detour, every trip takes longer over more kilometres.
Ordering elsewhere moves the lane's share of its site's orders to the other lanes into it, which ship only what their own sources hold or make.

scenarios.name: Fleet change
scenarios.description: The vehicles on some lanes change: drivers are short, or more are hired. Watch what the lanes carry, their utilisation and their costs.
effects: Each lane's fleet of each size is hired or released towards the new number over its hiring time; only idle vehicles are released.

scenarios.name: Demand surge
scenarios.description: Stores, customer areas or towns order more for a while, as on peak days. Watch warehouses and stores run down, vehicles fill up and orders wait.
effects: Each chosen site's demand rises by the share given, for the days given.

scenarios.name: Supplier short or late
scenarios.description: A supplier makes less than is ordered from it, takes longer over its orders, or both, for a while. Watch its orders wait to be made, the warehouses it supplies run down and the stores run out of what it makes.
effects: Short, the supplier makes only its share of what is ordered from it; the rest waits to be made, and arrives late.
Late, every order takes longer, those already in production too.
Its warehouses wait for it, or order what it cannot make from their other suppliers of the same goods.

scenarios.name: Site down
scenarios.description: A warehouse is out of action, or a store closed, for a while. Nothing goes into it or out of it by road, and nothing is sold or delivered from it. Watch the stores it restocks run down, or the sales a closed store loses.
effects: Every lane into the site and out of it is closed, and no order is placed over one; goods bound for it wait where they are.
Every delivery from its stock stops: a closed store's shoppers are lost or wait, as when its shelves are empty.
The sites it restocks wait for it, or order what it sent them from their other warehouses.
